products.name: Adobe Analytics
products.title: Adobe Analytics
products.what: Adobe's web and app analytics product. It collects data from sites and apps into report suites, and teams analyze that data in Analysis Workspace, with exports, alerts and reporting tools around it.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Analytics overview

products.notes: These lines cover a new or inherited Adobe Analytics setup: the solution design, report suites and variables, data collection through Web SDK and tags, Analysis Workspace, access and privacy labels, exports and a monthly service. New implementations are written for Web SDK with tags, the path Adobe's page calls the most direct; AN06 is for an organization that still runs the Analytics tag extension or AppMeasurement. Adobe describes Customer Journey Analytics as its next-generation analytics product and sells a one-time license for customers who move to it; the move itself is the existing CJA line CJ03 and the Adobe Analytics + Customer Journey Analytics connection, not a line here. Classification work uses classification sets, because Adobe's page says the older classification methods are being retired. Brand Visibility is not connected to Adobe Analytics in this tool, by Adam's decision. Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none.
prereqs: An Adobe Analytics license (Select, Prime or Ultimate), which sets how many variables and which features each report suite has
Access to Adobe Analytics granted to your client's administrators in the Admin Console
A solution design document agreed before the data layer and tags work starts
Site developers who build and maintain the data layer on your client's pages
For data feeds: a storage bucket on Amazon S3, Google Cloud Platform or Azure

prereq_sources.quote: Adobe Analytics Product(s) and Service(s) include but are not limited to Adobe Analytics (Foundation Pack for Experience Cloud, Select, Prime, and Ultimate), Adobe Analytics Evolution (Select, Prime, and Ultimate), and all applicable Add-ons.
Ensure that a system-level administrator has granted you access to Adobe Analytics via the CX Enterprise Admin Console.
Make sure that you are prepared with a solution design document before approaching development teams in your organization.
Your site development team is primarily responsible for making sure the data layer object populates with correct values.
A bucket configured on Amazon S3, Google Cloud Platform, Azure RBAC, or Azure SAS.

tiers.name: Adobe Analytics Select, Prime and Ultimate
tiers.what: The three packages Adobe sells. Each report suite has up to 75 props, 1,000 events and 150 processing rules on all three, 200 eVars on Select and Prime and 250 on Ultimate. Select does not include Contribution Analysis; Ultimate adds Cross-Device Analytics and a streaming media allowance.
tiers.quote: For purposes of clarity, Adobe Analytics - Select does not include a license to access or use and Customer agrees that it will not access or use Contribution Analysis

tiers.name: Adobe Analytics Foundation Pack for Experience Cloud
tiers.what: A volume-limited package that some AEM as a Cloud Service customers hold. Adobe no longer sells or renews it, and it has no Report Builder, Contribution Analysis, Customer Attributes or Advertising Analytics. Check which package your client holds before scoping AN04 and AN07.
tiers.quote: As such, as of January 1, 2024, Adobe is not offering any purchases, upsells, or renewals of this offering.

tiers.name: Adobe Analytics Evolution
tiers.what: A one-time license for a customer that is moving from Adobe Analytics to Customer Journey Analytics, with the same limits as the customer's earlier Adobe Analytics package. Where your client holds it, the move that line CJ03 covers is already under way.
tiers.quote: Adobe Analytics - Evolution is only available for licensing one time during the migration period from Adobe Analytics to Customer Journey Analytics and cannot be renewed.

lines.name: Solution design and measurement plan
lines.scope: Run KPI and business-question workshops with your client's stakeholders, map each requirement to a dimension or metric and its Analytics variable, and write the solution design document your client's team keeps current.
lines.evidence: A solution design document (also known as a solution design reference or business requirements document) is in essence the blueprint of your analytics implementation.

source.title: Experience League: Create a solution design document

lines.name: Report suites, variables and marketing channels
lines.scope: Create the development and production report suites, enable and name the conversion variables, success events and props from the solution design, add processing rules and bot rules, and configure marketing channels and classification sets for campaign tracking codes.
lines.evidence: Plan ahead by making a list of all your channels, so that all of your visitor hits are categorized to the right channel.

source.title: Experience League: Marketing Channel Manager

lines.name: Data layer and Web SDK data collection
lines.scope: Specify the data layer with your client's developers, set up the datastream, the tags property and the Web SDK extension, map data elements to Analytics variables, and validate in development before publishing to production.
lines.evidence: This implementation path is the most straightforward and typically the recommended path for new Web SDK implementations.

source.title: Experience League: Implement Adobe Analytics using the Web SDK tag extension

lines.name: Analysis Workspace projects and components
lines.scope: Build the agreed Analysis Workspace projects for your client's priority questions, with the segments, calculated metrics and alerts behind them, and save company templates the team reuses.
lines.evidence: Analysis Workspace allows you to build analyses quickly to gather insights and then share those insights with others.

source.title: Experience League: Analysis Workspace overview

lines.name: Access, privacy labels and team training
lines.scope: Set up product profiles in the Admin Console with the report suites, tools and components each team needs, assign identity and sensitivity labels to the report suite's variables, and train your client's analysts and business users on Analysis Workspace.
lines.evidence: Product profiles are permission presets that product admins can assign to users within an organization.

source.title: Experience League: Product profiles for Adobe Analytics

lines.name: Move an existing tags setup to Web SDK
lines.scope: Move your client's Adobe Analytics tag extension setup to the Web SDK with Adobe's upgrade assistant: choose the rules and data elements, map the Analytics variables to XDM, review the Web SDK actions it adds, then test the new library and compare reports before publishing.
lines.evidence: The Web SDK upgrade assistant helps you plan and execute the migration of your Adobe Analytics tags extension to the Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK.

source.title: Experience League: Web SDK upgrade assistant overview

lines.name: Data feeds and Data Warehouse exports
lines.scope: Set up the cloud account and location, create the hourly or daily data feed with the agreed columns, and schedule the Data Warehouse requests your client's data team needs.
lines.evidence: Data feeds are a powerful way to get raw data out of Adobe Analytics.

source.title: Experience League: Data feed overview

lines.ext: a cloud storage bucket on Amazon S3, Google Cloud Platform or Azure

lines.name: Monthly analysis and implementation review
lines.scope: Each month, analyze your client's priority journeys and campaigns and report findings and next steps, and after each site release check that the metrics and dimensions behind the top KPIs still collect correctly.
lines.evidence: If you consistently do this Focused Review after each website release, you'll find that your bi-annual Full Reviews are much easier.

source.title: Experience League: Focused Review (after each website release)

connections.how: Analytics for Target (A4T) makes Adobe Analytics the reporting source for a Target activity: Target sends the activity and experience a visitor saw to Analytics server to server, and every Analytics metric and segment is available on the activity's report in both products. Analytics can also supply the behavioral data for Target Recommendations.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Analytics for Target (A4T)

gain.title: One set of numbers for every test
gain.text: Your client's testing team and analysts read test results from the same data, so nobody reconciles two reports, and a metric or segment that was not chosen before the test started is still available after it ends.

flows.what: The activity and experience each visitor saw, and activity conversions, sent server to server on the same hit

source.title: Experience League: A4T reporting

flows.what: Analytics metrics, calculated metrics and segments, used as goal metrics and report audiences on the activity

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Analytics for Target (A4T)

flows.what: View-based and purchase-based behavioral data from product variables, as a daily feed for Recommendations criteria

source.title: Experience League: Use Adobe Analytics with Target Recommendations

gain.title: Storefront behavior in the reports the business already reads
gain.text: Product views, cart additions and orders from your client's Commerce store show up in Adobe Analytics without hand-built tagging on each storefront page.

flows.what: Storefront and order events, sent by the Data Connection extension through a datastream to the report suite

source.title: Experience League: Data Connection overview

connections.label: Commerce's Data Connection extension sends storefront events through a datastream to an Analytics report suite
connections.availability: Not stated by Adobe. The tutorial is written for Adobe Commerce cloud projects and says self-hosted projects can vary.

availability_source.quote: These instructions are for Adobe Commerce Cloud hosted projects. Self-hosted can vary to some degree, but the overall process should be similar.

prereqs: Adobe Commerce with the Data Connection extension installed and configured
Access to Adobe Analytics for the organization, and a report suite for the Commerce data
An XDM schema with the Adobe Analytics ExperienceEvent Commerce field group
A datastream with the Adobe Analytics service and the report suite ID

prereq_sources.quote: Follow the individual instructions here and return when completed to finish the remaining steps Install and configure the Experience Platform connector
Verify that your organization has (and you have) access to Adobe Analytics.
Select the Adobe Analytics ExperienceEvent Commerce by checking the box
Click Add Service and choose Adobe Analytics in the drop-down field.

lines.name: Commerce storefront events into a report suite
lines.scope: Install and configure the Data Connection extension with your client's Commerce team, build the schema with the Analytics commerce field group, create the datastream to the report suite, and check product, cart and order events in Analytics.
lines.evidence: Create a new report suite in Adobe Analytics, or identify the ID of the report suite that you will be pushing Commerce data into.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Analytics and Adobe Commerce integration tutorial

lines.name: Commerce reports in Analysis Workspace
lines.scope: Build your client's first commerce project in Analysis Workspace on the new data: product performance, cart and checkout fallout and revenue by marketing channel.
lines.evidence: Finally, to view your Commerce data, you will need to navigate to Analysis Workspace in Adobe Analytics, create a project, choose your report suite, and add freeform tables and other visualizations to report on and analyze your Commerce data.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Analytics and Adobe Commerce integration tutorial

client.how: An Adobe Commerce extension sends your storefront events, such as product views, cart additions and orders, through a datastream to your Adobe Analytics report suite.
client.gain: Your store's behavior shows up in the Adobe Analytics reports your business already reads, without hand-built tagging on each storefront page.

not_documented.why: Not found. The four pages linked from the Content Analytics overview in the Customer Journey Analytics guide do not name Adobe Analytics (0 mentions); Content Analytics is part of Customer Journey Analytics and reports from a CJA data view.

A developer note, not a setup. Brand Concierge's web client has an event callback that a page can use to send engagement data to Adobe Analytics or any other system; no page describes a Brand Concierge to Analytics configuration or what a report suite receives.
not_documented.quote: The event callback system lets a page observe Web Client lifecycle events, user interactions, responses, feedback, and errors in real time, useful for sending engagement data to Adobe Analytics, Google Analytics, or other third-party systems.

not_documented.why: One example in a list, no setup steps. Marketing Campaign Analytics accepts any Experience Platform dataset, and names data from the Analytics source connector as one example. The work is the source connector (XL04 on aa-rtcdp) plus the existing line XD09; a second card would repeat both.
not_documented.quote: Data collected using the Adobe Analytics source connector. And transformed into datasets conforming to the default or a custom version of the Adobe Analytics schema.

left_out.what: Adobe Analytics + AEM Forms (the aa-aemforms connection)
left_out.why: Already in the tool. The existing AEM Forms line AF09, Form analytics with Adobe Analytics, covers it and names Adobe Analytics as a product outside the tool. A second copy is not written; when aa joins the canvas, AF09 can move to an aa-aemforms card and lose its "Also needs" tag.

left_out.why: Adobe's table marks the in-product experience for Adobe Analytics as coming soon. XL16 and XL17 use the Coworker workspace, which the same table marks as available.

left_out.why: Adobe no longer sells or renews it. It is listed as a tier only so a partner checks what a client holds; the AEM Sites integration page still tells AEM customers they can ask for it.

left_out.what: Adobe Analytics 1.4 APIs and the older AEM Analytics frameworks
left_out.why: Shut down by Adobe. No line rests on them; XL11 and XL12 use IMS, server-to-server OAuth and the 2.0 API.
left_out.quote: Analytics 1.4 APIs August 31, 2026 Adobe Analytics 2.0 APIs

left_out.what: Labs in Adobe Analytics
left_out.why: Adobe describes Labs as early access to features under evaluation. Nothing is costed on it.

left_out.what: Audience Marketplace and third-party data in Audience Manager
left_out.why: Not a partner service: Adobe's sales specialist activates it and it handles the contracts and billing between data buyers and sellers. It also depends most on third-party cookies, which Adobe warns limit a data management platform. AU03 rebuilds segments on first-party traits.
left_out.quote: Talk to your Audience Manager sales specialist to get started. They can activate Audience Marketplace for you.

left_out.why: Discontinued by Adobe. AU06 uses authenticated profiles and hashed email, not the co-op device graph.
left_out.quote: All customers are expected to update any co-op Profile Merge Rules to utilize any options other than Device Co-op.

left_out.what: The older audience-sharing integration from Experience Platform to Audience Manager
left_out.why: Replaced by the self-service Experience Cloud Audiences destination, which XL06 and XL23 use. Where a client still has the older one, Adobe Customer Care disables it first; that is a prerequisite on aam-rtcdp, not a line.
left_out.quote: This destination replaces the legacy audience-sharing integration from Real-Time Customer Data Platform to various CX Enterprise solutions.

left_out.what: A new Audience Manager implementation
left_out.why: Adobe's implementation guide describes its own teams leading the phases, and Adobe now publishes a guide for moving to Real-Time CDP. The Audience Manager lines here are for a client that already runs it; this is a question for Adam.
left_out.quote: Getting started with Audience Manager can take approximately six weeks to three months, depending on your data collection needs.

left_out.what: Decommissioning Audience Manager at contract end
left_out.why: Adobe support publishes an article on switching off an instance, including the warning that Target can lose shared audiences. It is the last step of a move that XL21 plans; no separate line is costed until Adam decides whether the tool should sell it.
left_out.quote: The primary objective is to isolate Adobe Audience Manager and halt any inbound or outbound connections.

left_out.what: Role-based access controls and Audience Optimization reports in Audience Manager
left_out.why: Both must be switched on by Adobe for the organization. AU01 and AU07 use the general, trend and overlap reports and the standard user groups.
left_out.quote: Before you can use RBAC, this feature must be enabled by Adobe for your organization.

left_out.what: Streaming media analytics, Cross-Device Analytics, Live Stream and the Data Repair API
left_out.why: Documented, not costed in this pass. Each is an add-on or an Ultimate-only feature with its own implementation, outside the starting scope for a mid-market client.
left_out.quote: Adobe Analytics - Live Stream Add-on includes Live Stream triggers, Live Stream dashboards, and Live Stream data features.

for_other_helper.what: The Adobe Analytics connector sends email campaign indicators and attributes from Campaign v8 to Analytics (Web Analytics connectors add-on).

Experience Cloud Triggers: behaviors detected in Analytics, such as cart abandonment, reach Campaign through the pipeline and trigger emails. The Analytics product description allows rules-based triggers from Analytics to Campaign on every package.
Analytics integration guide pages for Campaign, and the Adobe Campaign setting in report suite admin.
Published Analytics segments reach Campaign with a further 24 hours of latency (stated on the segment publishing page).
Analytics for Advertising: click-through and view-through tracking in Analytics, and Analytics segments and events sent to Adobe Advertising.

Advertising Analytics in the Analytics integration guide (paid search data from Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising accounts in a report suite). This is search engine account data, not the Adobe Advertising product; listed so the other helper can rule it in or out.
B2B Customer Attributes: Marketo Measure uploads account and attributed revenue attributes to a Customer Attributes source that Analytics subscribes to.
Campaign imports shared audiences as lists and exports lists as shared audiences; Adobe provisions the integration.
Advertising DSP and Search, Social, & Commerce import Audience Manager segments for targeting; DSP can send media exposure data back.
The Experience Cloud Audiences page says Adobe strongly recommends the dedicated Campaign and Advertising DSP destination cards, and that those do not need an Audience Manager license.

lifecycle.question: Audience Manager: no end date from Adobe, but Adobe points customers to Real-Time CDP. How should the tool show it?

quotes.quote: There are no plans to modify the current Audience Manager Data Management Platform (DMP). However, the deprecation of third-party cookies will likely create scale challenges for most DMP users.
As your organization evolves to use Adobe Real-Time CDP, explore these considerations to prepare your data and to become aware of critical differences between the two technologies.

Adobe strongly recommends that segments activated in Audience Manager to people-based destinations get pushed to Real-Time CDP via the Audience Manager Source Connector, to then activate through Real-Time CDP.
Decommissioning Adobe Audience Manager (AAM) is a complex process that requires careful consideration of its impact on existing integrations and audience strategies.

lifecycle.found: Audience Manager is not on Adobe's list of discontinued products, and no page gives an end date. The Audience Manager guide's table of contents now opens with the guide to Real-Time CDP and two Web SDK migration pages. Adobe support publishes an article on switching an instance off at contract end. The sentence about no plans to modify sits on the Device Co-op end-of-life page.
lifecycle.recommendation: Show Audience Manager as one box, written for organizations that already run it. Its own services are a health check, Web SDK data collection, taxonomy, first-party onboarding, export controls and monthly operations; the move sits on the Audience Manager + Real-Time CDP card (XL21 to XL23). No card says the product is ending, because Adobe does not say so; the product note says Adobe publishes a guide for moving to Real-Time CDP.

lifecycle.question: Adobe Analytics: current, with Customer Journey Analytics described as the next generation and a one-time license for customers who move. Does any card need to say so?

quotes.quote: Customer Journey Analytics is Adobe's next-generation Analytics solution that lets you use the power of Analysis Workspace with data from Adobe Experience Platform.
Adobe Analytics - Evolution is designated for Customers migrating from Adobe Analytics Foundation, Select, Prime, or Ultimate to Customer Journey Analytics Foundation, Select, Prime, or Ultimate.
The Adobe Analytics Foundation Pack for Experience Cloud offering is designated for end-of-life status.
This information is especially valuable as you begin preparations to upgrade to Customer Journey Analytics.

lifecycle.found: No end date for Adobe Analytics on Experience League or helpx; the release notes are current and add features each month. Select, Prime and Ultimate are sold. Only the Foundation Pack is closed to purchases and renewals. The 1.4 API and the old Report Builder add-in are retired; nothing here rests on them.
lifecycle.recommendation: Show Adobe Analytics as a current product with no lifecycle wording. The upgrade story lives where it already does: the existing CJA line CJ03 and the new Adobe Analytics + Customer Journey Analytics card. The Evolution license and the Foundation Pack are listed as tiers so a partner checks what a client holds.

quotes.quote: The functionality described in this article is in the Limited Testing phase of release and might not be available yet in your environment.
This functionality will be deprecated after February 28, 2027.
You can't change the mappings, start, or end dates during the beta release.

lifecycle.found: Project migration with Coworker is in limited testing (left out; XL08 uses the Analytics interface). Coworker inside the Analytics interface is marked coming soon (left out; XL16 uses the Coworker workspace, marked available). Legacy classification methods are being retired (AN02 uses classification sets). One sentence on the Audience Manager page for Analytics destinations still mentions a beta release in the manual segment mapping step; the Audience Analytics pages carry no label, so XL19 is kept and uses automatic mapping.
lifecycle.recommendation: No action beyond what is written. If Adam reads the stale sentence on the Analytics destination page as a label, XL19 can drop manual segment mapping from its scope; it does not mention it today.

overlaps.existing: CJ03 Adobe Analytics upgrade to CJA
overlaps.note: CJ03 bundles the whole move: Web SDK beside the source connector, API and export changes, project migration. XL07 and XL08 are the two pieces a client needs when it keeps Adobe Analytics and adds CJA. A statement of work should carry CJ03 or these two, not both; CJ03 could move to the aa-cja card as its larger option.

overlaps.existing: TC03 A4T to CJA reporting transition; TG04 Recommendations catalog and setup
overlaps.note: TC03 moves a client off A4T and XL01 puts a client on it: opposite directions, so one statement of work should not carry both. XL03 feeds Recommendations from Analytics and assumes TG04 or an existing Recommendations setup.

overlaps.existing: RT02 Data sources and ingestion setup; XL07; XL09
overlaps.note: RT02 connects the agreed sources in general; XL04 is the Analytics source in particular. XL07 (CJA) and XL09 (journeys) each create the same source dataflow, and a report suite can have only one, so a statement of work with more than one of XL04, XL07 and XL09 should count the dataflow once.

overlaps.existing: AN03 Data layer and Web SDK data collection; AXA04 AEM page data collection for CJA; XA22 and XA24 on Edge Delivery
overlaps.note: XL11 and XL13 are the AEM-specific and Edge Delivery-specific parts of an Analytics implementation; with AN03 in scope they add the site-side setup only. XL11 documents Adobe's Analytics extension route, where AXA04 uses Web SDK for CJA. XL13 uses the same martech plugin as XA22 and XA24.

overlaps.existing: AF09 Form analytics with Adobe Analytics
overlaps.note: AF09 already covers the pair and carries an "Also needs Adobe Analytics" tag. No second copy.

overlaps.existing: EX04 Primary metrics from CJA or Adobe Analytics
overlaps.note: EX04 already covers the pair. No second copy.

overlaps.existing: XA17 Commerce data in CJA reports and the Commerce to Real-Time CDP lines
overlaps.note: All of them start from the Data Connection extension and a datastream. Where that is already in scope, XL14 adds only the Analytics service on the datastream and the report suite.

overlaps.existing: CW-CJA Coworker Skills for CJA reporting; XH01 and XH02 on Content Analytics
overlaps.note: The same Coworker analysis skills serve CJA and Adobe Analytics. A client with both needs one prompt and skill library, not two.

overlaps.existing: XB08 Share Marketo lists with Target
overlaps.note: XB08 sends Marketo lists to the Experience Cloud and uses them in Target; its card already says the lists reach Target through Audience Manager. XL25 is the same send, used in Audience Manager destinations. Count the organization mapping and the list send once.

overlaps.existing: RT04 Audience build and destination activation
overlaps.note: Rebuilding segments and reconnecting destinations in Real-Time CDP after the triage is RT04's work; XL21 to XL23 stop at the triage, the source connector and the audiences sent back.

overlaps.existing: AN06 Move an existing tags setup to Web SDK
overlaps.note: Adobe says an AppMeasurement to Web SDK move covers Analytics and Audience Manager together. XL18 is server-side forwarding on the current libraries; AU02 and AN06 are the Web SDK route. A statement of work should pick one route.
